docRequirement: context-window.md:29, the `Auto memory (MEMORY.md)` entry of the ContextWindow EVENTS array: "The first 200 lines or 25KB, whichever comes first, are loaded into the conversation context." MEMORY.md content that enters the conversation context must therefore be truncated at min(200 lines, 25KB) — two limits, whichever binds first. (The sibling `Project CLAUDE.md` entry at :76 carries only a tip, "Keep it under 200 lines", and binds nothing; the cap is auto-memory-specific.)
current:
The cap exists as a line-only cap on a branch that never runs in production, and the byte cap does not exist at all.

Legacy fallback (capped, dead): `packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-store.ts:8` declares `export const MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200;` and `memory-store.ts:29-33` `readMemoryFile(filePath, maxLines = MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT)` does `readFileSync(...).split(/\r?\n/).slice(0, maxLines)` — lines only, no byte budget. `readMemoryFileWithImports` (`memory-store.ts:66-110`) threads the same `maxLines` per file, and `loadMemoryPromptBlock` (`memory-store.ts:317-334`) is the only consumer. Covered by `packages/shared/src/agent/memory/__tests__/memory-store.test.ts:47-59` ('caps prompt reads to 200 lines').

That branch is gated off in production: `packages/shared/src/prompts/system.ts:453-455` reads `const memoryContext = capabilityContextPinned ? '' : loadMemoryPromptBlock(...)`, and both live agents pass `true` — `packages/shared/src/agent/pi-agent.ts:6607` and `packages/shared/src/agent/claude-agent.ts:1256` both hand `this.capabilityTurnRuntime !== null` into the `capabilityContextPinned` parameter (`system.ts:412`). The repo states this itself at `packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/__tests__/storage-runtime-fork-memory.test.ts:10-14` and in prose at `memory-store.ts:286-288`.

Live path (uncapped): `packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:976-977` loops `for (const layer of runtime.view.memory)` and does `const content = await runtime.materializer.readText(layer.resource);`. `packages/shared/src/capabilities/materializer.ts:169-187` is a whole-file read — `readFileSync(contentPath)` at `:181`, `content.toString('utf-8')` at `:186`, no slice. `base-agent.ts:997` then takes `const body = layer.format === 'rule' ? unscopedRuleBody(content) : content;`, strips only `@import` lines (`:1003-1007`) and pushes the remainder verbatim into the pinned block at `base-agent.ts:1014`, consumed uncut by `buildPinnedCapabilityContext` (`base-agent.ts:884-906`).

MEMORY.md genuinely is a memory layer on that path: `packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:909` (`~/.nessy/MEMORY.md`), `:978` (session MEMORY.md), `:1027` (`.nessy-agent/MEMORY.md`), `:1092` (project MEMORY.md) all call `memoryFileRecords`, which emits `kind: 'memory'` records at `native-sources.ts:404-424` and sets `memoryFormat` only for rule roots (`:416`); `packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:561-572` types `RuntimeMemoryHandle.format?: 'rule'`, and `packages/shared/src/capabilities/views.ts:218-220` pushes them into `view.memory`.

No byte limit exists anywhere on the load path. The only byte constant in the memory subsystem is `packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-cleanup.ts:33` `AUTO_MEMORY_CLEANUP_MAX_BYTES = 256 * 1024`, a guard that SKIPS cleanup of large files — the opposite of a load cap.

Aggravating: `base-agent.ts:944-957` (`forgetDeliveredPinnedCapabilityContext`) deliberately re-sends the pinned block after every compaction, quoting context-window.md's "Auto memory | Re-injected from disk" — so the uncapped body is re-injected each time.
divergence:
Two separate deltas, neither of them a naming or value mismatch.
(1) The 25KB limit is absent in every form — no constant, no check, on either path. Not a wrong key, not a wrong value: nothing implements the byte dimension.
(2) The 200-line limit is implemented with the correct value (`MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT = 200`) but only inside `readMemoryFile`, which `system.ts:453-455` bypasses whenever a capability runtime exists — i.e. on every turn of both shipping backends. On the path that actually feeds the model, `base-agent.ts:976-1014`, neither limit is applied, so a MEMORY.md of arbitrary size enters context whole. Observable production behaviour is therefore 'no cap', which contradicts the page rather than narrowing it; the correct-valued cap sitting on the dead branch is why this reads as partial from the constant alone.

change.what: Add `export const MEMORY_LOAD_BYTE_LIMIT = 25 * 1024;` beside `MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT` at :8, citing context-window.md:29. Add an exported pure helper `export function capMemoryContent(text: string, maxLines = MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT, maxBytes = MEMORY_LOAD_BYTE_LIMIT): string` that (a) keeps the first `maxLines` lines, then (b) accumulates lines while `Buffer.byteLength(candidate, 'utf-8') <= maxBytes`, dropping from the first line that would cross — 'whichever comes first' means both are applied and the tighter wins — and returns `.trim()` to match today's shape. Rewrite `readMemoryFile` (:29-33) to `readFileSync(filePath, 'utf-8')` then `return capMemoryContent(raw, maxLines)` so the legacy fallback gains the byte dimension without changing its line behaviour. Do NOT touch `readMemoryFileWithImports`'s per-file threading (:66-110) — per-file capping is the existing semantics and is what the pinned path should match.

One line, at :997. Change `const body = layer.format === 'rule' ? unscopedRuleBody(content) : content;` to `const body = layer.format === 'rule' ? unscopedRuleBody(content) : capMemoryContent(content);`, plus the import of `capMemoryContent` from `./memory/memory-store.ts` (the file already imports `parseMemoryImportPath` and `unscopedRuleBody` from that area). Cap BEFORE the `@import`-line strip at :1003-1007 so the truncation point matches the legacy path, which capped the raw file and only then expanded imports. Leave rule layers alone: the page's cap is scoped to auto memory, and a `paths:` rule's body is already gated by match. Leave `runtime.view.promptLayers` (:966-975, the AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md family) uncapped — context-window.md:76 gives CLAUDE.md a `tip`, not a limit.

Decide explicitly, do not let it change by accident. `:427` calls `readMemoryFile(resolvedPath)` with defaults purely to discover `@import` lines, so a new default byte cap would silently stop registering imports declared past 25KB. Either pass an explicit opt-out (`readMemoryFile(resolvedPath, MEMORY_LOAD_LINE_LIMIT, Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY)`) to keep the discovered record set byte-for-byte identical, or accept the narrowing deliberately and note it — because the record set is hashed into the capability snapshot and a change here moves the generation id for every user with a >25KB MEMORY.md.

Add one sibling case: write a MEMORY.md of ~40 short-line KB under 200 lines (e.g. 150 lines of 300 bytes) and assert `Buffer.byteLength(readMemoryFile(filePath)) <= 25 * 1024` and that the last surviving line is a whole line. Keep the existing 200-line case as the other half of 'whichever comes first'.

Add the regression that would have caught this: build a turn runtime whose `view.memory` holds one non-rule layer backed by a 250-line MEMORY.md, run the pinned-context builder, and assert the emitted `<capability-layer …>` body is 200 lines and under 25KB. This is the test the subsystem lacks — the only existing cap test exercises the dead branch.

blastRadius: `readMemoryFile` has four call sites: `memory-store.ts:77` (inside `readMemoryFileWithImports`, feeding `loadMemoryPromptBlock` and `loadUnscopedRuleMemories` at :295), and `native-sources.ts:427` (capability-snapshot import discovery). The second one crosses a persistence boundary: `memoryFileRecords` records carry `revision`/`contentHash` (`native-sources.ts:420-423`) and feed the capability snapshot whose `generation` gates the pinned-context cache (`base-agent.ts:889-892`), so changing which imports are discovered changes snapshot content and forces a generation change — a risk trigger under this repo's rules. The `base-agent.ts:997` edit sits on the path every backend turn takes (`buildPinnedCapabilityContext` at :884, `takePinnedCapabilityContextForTurn` at :917, re-injection at :954) and is shared by Pi (`pi-agent.ts:6607` context) and Claude (`claude-agent.ts:1256` context) alike. It also touches the `InstructionsLoaded` emission at `base-agent.ts:1009-1013` and :1043-1046 only indirectly — an entirely-empty capped body would hit the `if (!withoutImports) continue;` guard at :1008 and drop the eager event for that file, which is correct but should be checked. Nothing on the wire schema changes: `RuntimeMemoryHandle` (`resolver.ts:561-572`) and `views.ts:218-220` keep their shapes; the cap is applied to already-materialized text. Imported-plugin paths are unaffected — plugin bundles come through `materializer.readText`'s `pluginInstanceId` branch (`materializer.ts:171-178`) and are prompt/skill layers, not memory layers. Existing tests that would need review: `packages/shared/src/agent/memory/__tests__/memory-store.test.ts`, `packages/server-core/src/bootstrap/__tests__/storage-runtime-fork-memory.test.ts`, and any base-agent fixture asserting a full pinned block string.
userImpact: Concrete but quiet. Any user whose `MEMORY.md` (global `~/.nessy/MEMORY.md`, the project one, `.nessy-agent/MEMORY.md`, or the per-session file) has grown past 200 lines or 25KB has every byte of it injected into the pinned capability block on every turn of both shipping backends, and re-injected after each compaction (`base-agent.ts:944-957`). What they see is not an error but a budget: higher input token usage per turn, earlier auto-compaction, and — for a file near the 256KB the cleanup guard tolerates (`memory-cleanup.ts:33`) — tens of thousands of tokens per turn of memory they were told would be trimmed at 200 lines. The documented guidance ('keep it under 200 lines, the rest is dropped') is silently false here in the generous direction, so nobody hits a wall; they just pay. It would surface immediately in a token-usage readout comparing a 200-line and a 2000-line MEMORY.md on the same prompt, or in the context-usage indicator after adding a large memory file.

Scope caveat carried forward from the challenger: this is the same underlying defect already filed against memory.md; this page restates it as a context-budget guarantee, so land one fix and mark both rows.
